text: Section 929P(b) risks complications where the SEC proceeds unilaterally in situations in which coordinated enforcement with foreign regulators would be more effective, for example insider trading cases involving exchanges whose home regimes do not recognize comparable insider trading rules.
citation: Kaal and Painter, The Aftermath of Morrison v. National Australia Bank and Elliott Associates v. Porsche (2011). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1765901

isBasedOn.name: The Aftermath of Morrison v. National Australia Bank and Elliott Associates v. Porsche

abstract: The provision risks complications if the SEC pursues cases unilaterally when coordinated enforcement with foreign regulators would be more effective.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: unilateral SEC enforcement over foreign exchange transactions
